title: Data-source registry — every symbolic and stem source audited for the styles PDMX cannot supply (Wave Q, PR-76)

method.classification: classifyDataSource (dataSourceRegistry.ts): non-commercial or AI-training-ban wording in any of the three layers or the stated restriction → BLOCKED_LICENSE; underlying works not cleared → RESEARCH_ONLY; any layer unread or works unknown → LEGAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED; else TRAIN_CLEARED. Derived, never stored.
method.yield: estimateTaskYield: a work yields tasks at PR-65's measured PDMX rate for its ensemble shape (65.30 per multitrack work, of which 49.41 arrangement tasks; 9.73 per solo/melody work; 0 for drums-only, audio stems and theory). Sizes are the sources' claims unless measured=true.

sources.name: PDMX — no_license_conflict subset
sources.why: PDMX — no_license_conflict subset: compilation, per-work and underlying-works layers are each verified from a primary source and none is restrictive.

claimedSize.claim: 222,856 admitted rows, 222,820 with a MIDI file; 20,638 multitrack works, 19,588 independent after near-duplicate collapse (PR-65, measured on every file)

yieldEstimate.assumption: 222820 claimed works, 9 % assumed multitrack (a claim), PDMX rates for each share

cost.note: already acquired under PR-51; 469 MB verified against Zenodo md5

compilation.stated: cc-by-4.0 (Zenodo record licence) — covers the compilation, not the works inside it
compilation.source: Zenodo record 15571083 via the public API, recorded in docs/evidence/pdmx-acquisition-live.json (PR-51)

perWork.stated: PDMX.csv `license` column, public domain / CC0 / cc-zero per row, admitted only when the authors' `license_conflict` flag is clear — read on all 254,077 rows

underlyingWorks.stated: The uploader's public-domain / CC0 dedication on MuseScore, cross-checked by the authors against the file's own metadata; rows where the two disagree are excluded
underlyingWorks.source: PDMX paper (arXiv 2409.10831) and the subset flag, applied per row in PR-51

rightsRecordNeeds: exists: work id, licence string, license_conflict flag, authors' subset membership, dataset and rights digests (datasetRightsProof.ts)
knownLimitations: Residual: an uploader can dedicate an arrangement of a copyrighted song as public domain; PDMX verifies the metadata agreement, not the composition rights. PR-60 found the corpus's 'pop' is largely piano-vocal transcription — this residual is what that is.
3,197 labelled non-classical multitrack works, 0 Mizrahi/Israeli (PR-65). This is the gap the rest of this registry exists to fill.

sources.name: Groove MIDI Dataset (GMD)
sources.why: Groove MIDI Dataset (GMD): compilation, per-work and underlying-works layers are each verified from a primary source and none is restrictive.
regions: USA (studio); genre labels afrobeat, afrocuban, highlife, latin, middleeastern, reggae, hiphop, dance, funk, gospel, soul, punk, rock, pop, jazz, blues, country, neworleans

claimedSize.claim: 1,150 MIDI files, 13.6 hours, ~22,000 measures, 445,494 hits, 10 drummers (dataset page)

yieldEstimate.assumption: drums only: no harmonic context, no arrangement task; usable as a groove prior, not as a task source

compilation.stated: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), made available by Google LLC

perWork.stated: uniform — one licence for the whole release; no per-file variation

underlyingWorks.stated: Performances recorded by Google on a Roland TD-11 by ten drummers, 'more than 80% of duration coming from hired professionals', following a metronome — original performances, no transcribed works

rightsRecordNeeds: file id, drummer id, genre label, CC BY 4.0 attribution string, release version
knownLimitations: Drums only: no pitched context, so it cannot form an arrangement task by itself. Its value is as a groove prior (the afrobeat/reggae/latin/middleeastern grooves are the only cleared production-style material in this whole registry).
Genre labels are the drummers' own session labels — 'middleeastern' is a Western studio drummer's idea of it, not a darbuka player's.

sources.name: Radif Corpus (Mīrzā ʿAbdollāh radif, Iranian classical)
sources.why: Radif Corpus (Mīrzā ʿAbdollāh radif, Iranian classical): compilation, per-work and underlying-works layers are each verified from a primary source and none is restrictive.
regions: Iran (dastgāh system — a neighbour of Arabic/Turkish maqam, not the same system)

claimedSize.claim: 228 non-metric gūshehs, 43,441 notes, ~281 minutes; MIDI, CSV and MusicXML (paper)

yieldEstimate.assumption: 228 claimed works × PDMX solo rate (9.73 per work); melody_only yields no arrangement task — nothing to hide

compilation.stated: 'All materials are released under a CC-BY 4.0 license, allowing for reuse and adaptation with proper credit.'
compilation.source: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.10456v1 (full text); Zenodo record 15742125 answered 504 on the day

perWork.stated: uniform — one licence statement for all materials

underlyingWorks.stated: Mīrzā ʿAbdollāh's radif (d. 1918), transcribed from Dariush Talai's edition 'Radif Analysis' — the repertoire is traditional and public domain by age

rightsRecordNeeds: gūsheh id, dastgāh, CC BY attribution, note that the transcription derives from Talai's edition (residual: edition rights, see limitations)
knownLimitations: Residual: Talai's edition is a modern copyrighted book; the dataset authors' CC BY release covers their transcription, and the underlying repertoire is PD by age — the edition's own typographic/editorial rights are a residual to note, not a block.
Monophonic and non-metric: zero arrangement tasks. Its use is a modal/melodic prior for the Middle-Eastern family, not production material.
Dastgāh is not maqam: related interval theory, different repertoire and practice.
